title: 3.2 A 36V Current-Balancing Instrumentation Amplifier with ±24V Input Range, 5.6MHz BW, and 140dB CMRR at All Gain Settings
problem: Industrial instrumentation amplifiers must handle large differential input ranges (>20V) with large common-mode input offsets (±10V), require high CMRR (>120dB), high input impedance (>10MΩ), and wide bandwidth while processing millivolt-level signals from sensors.
motivation: Industrial control systems with distributed sensors and varying ground potentials require integrated gain-adjustable instrumentation amplifiers with large CM input ranges and superior rejection across all gain settings.
method: 36V high-voltage instrumentation amplifier with current-balancing architecture enabling ±24V differential input range and ±10V CM input handling. Direct coupling with carefully designed gain stages maintains 140dB CMRR across all gain settings.
key_novelty: Current-balancing topology achieving 140dB CMRR at all gain settings without requiring separate higher supply voltage for CM rejection.
contributions: ±24V differential input range with ±10V CM input handling
140dB CMRR maintained across all gain settings
Gain-adjustable architecture for sensor signal conditioning
primary_theme: high-voltage instrumentation amplifier with superior CMRR
